summary:
Prometheus is a web platform for exploring fire activity across time and understanding differences between MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations. We developed a data pipeline, a machine-learning harmonization layer, and an interactive dashboard that brings their outputs together.

Our Model B uses MODIS-derived information to score candidate cells against a VIIRS detection reference. The dashboard keeps these uncalibrated model estimates separate from observed hotspots, preserving their sources and scientific limitations.

Users can select a country, region, and date range; inspect satellite records on a map; explore a burning activity calendar; compare seasonal patterns and countries; and download CSV data and PDF reports. Verified datasets are delivered through Azure storage, with Morocco and Algeria currently available.

By making satellite fire data easier to explore and compare, Prometheus helps researchers and land managers investigate historical burning patterns while clearly distinguishing missing coverage, recorded observations, and model estimates.
